routes.label: Construct one repeated zero with the required constant terms

question: Suppose that \(P(z),\) \(Q(z),\) and \(R(z)\) are polynomials with real coefficients, having degrees \(2,\) \(3,\) and \(6,\) respectively, and constant terms \(1,\) \(2,\) and \(3,\) respectively. Let \(N\) be the number of distinct complex numbers \(z\) that satisfy the equation \[P(z) \cdot Q(z) = R(z).\] What is the minimum possible value of \(N?\)
solution:
The equation is equivalent to setting one degree-six polynomial equal to zero. Its roots may repeat, so six roots counted with multiplicity need not mean six distinct solutions.

Let
\[
D(z)=R(z)-P(z)Q(z).
\]
The product \(P(z)Q(z)\) has degree \(2+3=5\), so it cannot cancel the degree-six term of \(R(z)\). Thus \(D\) has degree \(6\). By the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra, every nonconstant polynomial has at least one complex zero. Hence \(N\ge1\).

To attain this bound, choose
\[
P(z)=z^2+1,\qquad Q(z)=z^3+2,
\]
and define
\[
R(z)=P(z)Q(z)+(z-1)^6.
\]
These polynomials have real coefficients and the required degrees. The constant term of \(R\) is \(1\cdot2+(-1)^6=3\), as required.

For this choice, the original equation reduces to
\[
(z-1)^6=0,
\]
whose only distinct solution is \(z=1\). Therefore the minimum is \(\boxed{1}\), choice \(\textbf{B}\).
